subject: Materials Science
title: Gold Nanoparticles: Ancient Color, Modern Medicine
description: A quick, practical guide to Gold Nanoparticles: Ancient Color, Modern Medicine.

hook.text: The Lycurgus Cup glows red with transmitted light — Roman glassmakers embedded gold nanoparticles 1,700 years ago.

buildup.text: Gold nanoparticles absorb and scatter light via surface plasmon resonance — electrons oscillating at set frequencies.

discovery.text: 20 nm gold particles appear ruby red, 100 nm ones look blue — size tunes the plasmon resonance wavelength.

twist.text: Gold nanoparticles aren't just pretty — the red line in COVID rapid tests is colloidal gold bound to antibodies.

climax.text: In cancer therapy, gold nanorods absorb infrared light and heat tumors — photothermal therapy at nanoscale.

punchline.text: Romans used gold nanoparticles for art — we use them to fight disease.

quiz.question: What causes gold nanoparticles to appear red?
options: They are coated with red dye
Surface plasmon resonance absorbs specific wavelengths based on particle size
Gold naturally becomes red at small sizes due to melting
